rows.evidence: Q1: Methodology and Optimization Results sections <U+2013> the authors run their own CWRF regional climate model ensembles (five physics configurations, 15-day forecasts, 2002<U+2013>2006), bias-correct them, and couple them to a SWAP-based daily simulation-optimization of irrigation for the Havana Lowlands, Illinois; Figs. 6<U+2013>9 report the resulting simulated irrigation amounts, yields and profits.
rows.notes: The study is a pure simulation-optimization exercise. The 4<U+2013>6% water reduction and 1<U+2013>3% profit gain cited in the passage (Abstract; Optimization Results; Conclusions) are differences between modelled scenarios (imperfect RCM forecasts vs. a no-rain baseline, and vs. average climatology), generated by a SWAP crop model calibrated in earlier work (Wang and Cai 2007). Only the weather forecasts were checked against observations (bias correction, skill scores, Fig. 5); the outputs on which the claim rests (irrigation water use, profit) were never compared with measured irrigation or yields from the real system, so under the rating rules this does not count as own evidence on the claimed effect. The authors themselves describe the result as an upper limit because the RCM is driven by reanalysis rather than real forecasts. Also, the passage mentions forecasts of rainfall and ETo, whereas the study forecasts rainfall and min/max temperature and replaces humidity, wind and radiation with climatology. The study does report dispersion (ensemble spread, Figs. 10<U+2013>12), stated limitations (reanalysis-driven upper limit, single site, 5 years, case-dependent assumptions) and a condition (gains higher when water is limited), but these are not credited because Q2 is 'no'. Technology label 'app_scheduling' is a loose fit for a research simulation-optimization decision framework, but the passage describes the study accurately so no technology mismatch is flagged.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Study is a modelling case study at a single region (Havana Lowlands/Mason County, Illinois), corn, five seasons 2002<U+2013>2006, sprinkler irrigation; results are simulated scenario comparisons without field validation of water use or profit.
